NoteTexAccessor::greek¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch NoteTexAccessor::greek() const

Classify Lowercase Greek Control Words¶

greek() finds recognized lowercase Greek-letter commands inside complete math fragments and returns their names without the leading backslash. It recognizes the standard lowercase sequence from alpha through omega, plus the variant forms varepsilon, vartheta, and varphi.

The operation deliberately distinguishes TeX commands from prose and from literal Unicode letters. Plain alpha, the character α, and \alpha outside math are not tokens. Uppercase commands are not silently folded to lowercase. Use symbols() when all control words are wanted, not only this semantic vocabulary.

All four anonymous math delimiter forms are scanned. Escaped or unmatched delimiters do not open math. Tokens keep document order and duplicates; the ragged TokenBatch offsets retain each cell’s range. Undefined input propagates, and non-text input throws.

Example 1: Commands, Prose, And Empty Lanes¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note(
    std::vector<std::string>{
        R"(prose 99; $x_1 + \sin(\alpha) = 2.5$)",
        R"(\[\beta \leq y^2\] and \(\sqrt{z}\))",
        R"(escaped \$7 and plain theta)",
        R"($$\argmax_x f(x) \approx 10$$)"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
const auto result = source.tex().greek();
std::cout << result.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["alpha", "beta"]

Example 2: Offsets Preserve The Empty Third Cell¶

const auto offsets = result.offsets().integers();
for (auto value : offsets) std::cout << value << ' ';
std::cout << '\n';

Output¶

0 1 2 2 2

Example 3: Dtype Boundary¶

try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1}).tex().greek();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "Greek commands Int64: rejected\n"; }

Output¶

Greek commands Int64: rejected

See Also¶

  • symbols: collect every TeX control word and operator symbol.

  • ids: collect broad identifier lexemes without semantic classification.
